chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayyoub, from Muhammad ibn Sowqat, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: 'So whoever alters it after he has heard it, then the sin is upon those who alter it.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'It was abrogated by the verse that follows it, His Words, the Mighty and Majestic: 'But he who fears from the testator an inclination to a wrong course or an act of disobedience, and makes peace between them, then there is no blame on him.'

He said: 'It means the executor; if he fears injustice from the testator regarding what he bequeathed to him, from that which Allah is not pleased with, being contrary to the right, then there is no blame on him, i.e., upon the executor, to alter it to the right and to that which Allah is pleased with, from the way of goodness.'

key_terms.الْمُوصَى إِلَيْهِ: The executor (person to whom the will is addressed)
key_terms.جَنَفاً: Inclination to a wrong course / injustice
key_terms.نَسَخَتْهَا: Abrogated it (rendered it inapplicable by a later verse)

ai.seo_question: How does the executor correct a will if the testator's bequest is unjust or contrary to God's pleasure?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the general prohibition against altering a will is abrogated by the specific provision allowing correction when injustice or sin is feared, establishing a principle of pragmatic flexibility in estate management. This ruling empowers the executor to modify the bequest to align with divine pleasure, ensuring that the testator's intent does not lead to religious or moral error, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the preservation of justice in legal instruments.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad Bin Sowqat who said,
‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about the Words of Allahazwj Blessed and High [2:181] So the one who alters it after he has heard it, the sin of it then is only upon the one who alters it.

Heasws said: ‘It has to be considered by the Verse, which is after it, the Words of the Mighty and Majestic [2:182] But he who fears an inclination to a wrong course or an act of disobedience on the part of the testator, and effects an agreement between the parties, there is no blame on him.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It means the executor, if he fears injustice on the part of the testator with regards to what he has bequeathed with to him from what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is not Pleased with, being opposite to the right, so there is no blame upon him, i.e., upon the executor, that he changes it to the right and to what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is Pleased with, from the way of the Goodness’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Sawqah who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the meaning of the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘Whoever intentionally changes the will of a deceased person, has committed a sin. Allah is All-hearing and All-knowing. 5 [2:181]

He (the Imam) said, ‘The following verse is a (modified) copy of this verse: ‘One who is afraid of the testator’s deviations and sin and settles the matter among the parties involved, he has not committed a sin. Allah is All-forgiving and All- merciful. 5 [2:182]

If the executor fears for the testator’s deviation from the law in his will, then it is not a sin for the executor to bring it in conformity with the truth according to the happiness of Allah and following the path of virtue. 555
